title: arXiv physics daily — latest announcement batch: 2 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This is an inferred ranking with limited citation evidence for such recent papers; it is not a most-read, most-downloaded, or consensus ranking.

sections.title: Preparation of a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator on a superconducting quantum processor
sections.abstract: The authors prepare a bosonic Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator and a two-quasihole state on an IBM superconducting processor, finding measured densities, correlations, and chiral currents consistent with the target states.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report preparation on an IBM Nighthawk 4×4 qubit patch of a four-boson FCI state and a three-boson state with two quasiholes; density/correlation measurements and reconstructed currents show the expected chiral pattern.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; quantum-circuit execution on IBM Nighthawk, with exact diagonalization and classical variational circuit optimization.
sections.unique_caveat: The target states remain classically accessible at this 4×4 size, and the authors identify classical target-state preparation as a scalability limitation; this is not a demonstration of anyon braiding.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across quantum information and two condensed-matter categories; a topic-specific Quantum Physics Papers X post surfaced. The post is an attention signal, not scientific validation.

sections.title: Control-Noise Trade-offs in Industrially Integrated ${}^{28}\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{SiGe}$ Spin-1/2 Qubits
sections.abstract: The authors compare industry-fabricated silicon spin qubits with a research-cleanroom reference and report near-99.99% primitive π/2-gate fidelities alongside a micromagnet-placement trade-off between noise sensitivity and drive efficiency.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report primitive π/2-gate fidelities near 99.99% in Intel 300 mm-process devices, with reduced low-frequency noise and variability but weaker electrically driven spin-resonance gradients than the RIKEN reference.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; measurements on two nominally similar three-qubit Intel Si/SiGe devices, compared with a research-cleanroom reference device.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison covers a small device sample, not a processor-scale array; the paper also finds drive-dependent errors at lower Rabi frequencies, so the reported primitive-gate fidelity is not fault-tolerant processor performance.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listing bridges quantum information and mesoscopic physics; a field-specific preprint meeting listing and the quantified gate/control results provide corroborating visibility and a concrete technical result.

sections.title: Magnetic Johnson noise from arbitrarily shaped conductors: experimental validation of the fluctuation-dissipation finite-element method
sections.abstract: Using a SQUID gradiometer array, the authors find that a fluctuation-dissipation finite-element calculation reproduces measured magnetic Johnson-noise amplitudes and frequency dependence for conductors with complex shapes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report agreement between SQUID-array measurements and COMSOL finite-element calculations for complex conductors, including noise amplitude and spectral shape; agreement at high frequency is weaker for a combined-gradiometer comparison.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; SQUID gradiometer measurements compared with COMSOL calculations for an aluminum plate and a commercial aluminum corner bracket.
sections.unique_caveat: The sample temperature was not measured and typical conductivities were assumed; the combined-gradiometer comparison retains an unresolved high-frequency discrepancy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in five physics categories spanning applied physics, nuclear experiment, atomic physics, biological physics, and detectors; a third-party technical summary also surfaced. The breadth reflects method relevance, not independent confirmations.

sections.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
sections.abstract: Field-resolved pump-probe measurements of germanium at 5 μm yield an instantaneous Kerr response and a nonlinear refractive index of n₂=(0.87±0.16)×10⁻¹⁷ m²/W.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find that the measured cross-phase modulation follows the pump envelope and disappears when pump and probe cease to overlap, supporting an instantaneous Kerr response under their conditions.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy of germanium at 5 μm.
sections.unique_caveat: The result establishes the dominant contribution only for the tested germanium sample and experimental conditions; it does not establish the same balance of instantaneous and delayed effects in other semiconductors or regimes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed between optics and materials science, with a topic-specific optics X post; the directly time-resolved measurement and reported uncertainty provide a checkable result.

sections.title: A first look at strange-quark polarization in top-quark decays with CMS Open Data
sections.abstract: An analysis of 16.39 fb⁻¹ of public 13 TeV CMS data measures longitudinal Λ polarization in strange jets from semileptonic top-pair events, but the result is consistent with both zero and the LEP-inferred transfer.
sections.claimed_result: The author reports P_parallel=+0.04±0.45 (stat.)±0.06 (syst.) for the high-momentum-fraction sample, consistent with zero and with the transfer inferred from LEP; the paper presents it as a first analysis-chain realization, not a resolved polarization measurement.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; analysis of 2016 CMS Open Data from 13 TeV proton-proton collisions, using 16.39 fb⁻¹.
sections.unique_caveat: Statistical precision is insufficient to test the polarization transfer; the paper identifies background and acceptance systematics that need data-driven treatment in a higher-statistics measurement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listing links collider experiment and phenomenology; the analysis uses the public CMS collision-data release and opens a direct route to follow-up with larger Run-2/Run-3 samples. Search also surfaced an arXiv hep-ex feed post.

sections.title: Vacuum amplification across a programmable bosonic Bogoliubov stability boundary in a trapped-ion chain
sections.abstract: The authors tune two motional-mode couplings in a trapped-ion chain and observe bounded phonon occupation below a programmable stability threshold and exponential amplification above it, including resonant single-mode squeezing.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report independent control of pair creation and mode splitting and demonstrate that the amplification threshold can be moved, including a resonant regime where one mode is amplified into a squeezed vacuum.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; motional modes of a trapped-ion chain, initialized near the motional ground state.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration concerns a controlled two-mode system; proposed connections to particle creation and driven-device operation remain applications, not observations of those phenomena in other systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across quantum and atomic physics; this is an experimental test of a programmable threshold rather than only a proposed analogue, making the controlled two-mode result a concrete signal in the batch.

sections.title: Soft X-Ray Detection Down to the Nitrogen K-Edge Using a Pixelated iLGAD Sensor
sections.abstract: Pixelated inverse low-gain avalanche-diode sensors with a thin entrance window resolve single soft-X-ray photons down to 390 eV, below the nitrogen K-edge, with a reported signal-to-noise ratio of 5.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report single-photon resolution to 390 eV and use the observed double-peak response to fit effective entrance-layer and gain-layer depths.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; spectral characterization of two iLGAD gain-layer designs across photon energies and operating temperatures.
sections.unique_caveat: The study characterizes sensor designs rather than demonstrating a large-area, high-frame-rate detector in a beamline experiment; those application-level performance claims remain prospective.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A quantified low-energy single-photon threshold and a comparison of standard versus shallow gain-layer designs provide a concrete instrumentation result; it is retained as a notable detector paper despite having no cross-list in the checked metadata.

sections.title: Gapless and Non-Equilibrium Topology in Blockaded Ladders
sections.abstract: The authors propose constrained multi-leg models with gapless topological order and long-lived post-quench string order, supported by tensor-network simulations and a classical stochastic approximation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors argue that blockade constraints can produce gapless topological ground states and preserve string order for parametrically long post-quench times in two-leg models; three-leg models yield a multicomponent Luttinger liquid.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical and computational; tensor-network simulations and a classical stochastic approximation to the dynamics.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposed mechanism and dynamical signatures have not been experimentally established in a Rydberg or dipolar-atom platform.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across four physics categories and connects constrained many-body theory with candidate Rydberg/dipolar-atom simulator platforms; the result is a theoretically grounded platform proposal, not an experimental detection.
